chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Amr ibn Ibrahim, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Umar ibn Aban, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who drinks an intoxicant, it becomes a right upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that He quenches him from the essence of Khabal.' I said, 'And what is the essence of Khabal?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Puss from the private parts of a prostitute.'

key_terms.طِينَةُ خَبَالٍ: Essence of Khabal (a specific impure fluid)

ai.seo_question: What is the specific punishment for wine drinkers in the afterlife according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a specific divine recompense for wine drinkers, linking the physical act of drinking to a tangible, albeit grotesque, punishment in the afterlife. The definition of 'Khabal' as the pus of prostitutes' private parts serves as a precise anatomical counterpart to the drinker's consumption, reflecting the Shia scholarly tradition of detailed eschatological descriptions. This narration underscores the concept of *haqq Allah* (a right due to God) being fulfilled through direct, physical retribution rather than mere spiritual abstraction.
